learn.hook: Some deserts burn hot with golden sand. Others are freezing cold with snowy mountains! India has both kinds.
points: A desert is a place that gets very little rain.
The Thar Desert is a hot desert, mostly in Rajasthan. It has sand dunes, very hot days and cool nights. Jaisalmer is a city in the Thar.
Ladakh is a cold desert. It is high in the mountains, gets very little rain, and has freezing winters.
The camel is called the 'ship of the desert'. Its wide, padded feet do not sink in sand, and its hump stores fat, not water. In Ladakh's Nubra Valley there are two-humped camels.
The Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is a huge salt desert. In winter it shines white like snow.

example.q: Think it through: why do houses in the Thar Desert often have thick mud walls?
steps: Days in the desert are very hot.
Thick mud walls do not let heat in quickly.
So the inside of the house stays cooler during the day.
example.answer: Thick mud walls keep the house cool in the hot desert.

learn.reallife: Many people visit the Rann Utsav in Kutch in winter and enjoy camel rides on the dunes near Jaisalmer.

games.title: Desert detective
items: A camel stores water in its hump.
The hump stores fat. The camel can use this fat when food is scarce.
A desert gets very little rain.
Low rainfall is what makes a place a desert.
Ladakh is high, very cold and gets very little rain.
The Rann of Kutch is a salt desert in Gujarat.
It is covered with white salt in the dry season.
Deserts never have any plants or animals.
Cactus, khejri trees, camels, foxes and lizards live in deserts.

quiz.q: What makes a place a desert?
options: It is always near the sea
quiz.explain: Deserts are dry because they get very little rain. They can be hot or cold.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all deserts must be hot

quiz.q: The Thar Desert is mostly in which state?
quiz.explain: Most of the Thar Desert lies in western Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where India's hot desert is

quiz.q: Why is Ladakh called a cold desert?
options: It is full of hot sand
It is very cold and gets very little rain
quiz.explain: Ladakh is high in the mountains, so it is cold, and it gets very little rain.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a desert must be sandy and hot

quiz.q: What does a camel's hump store?
quiz.explain: The hump stores fat, which the camel can use for energy when food is scarce.
quiz.mistake: Believes the common myth that the hump holds water

quiz.q: How do a camel's feet help it walk on sand?
options: They are wide and padded, so they don't sink
They have sharp claws to dig
quiz.explain: Wide, padded feet spread the camel's weight, so it does not sink into soft sand.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect body parts with how animals live

quiz.q: Which place is a white salt desert?
quiz.explain: The Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is covered with a crust of white salt.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the salt desert with sandy or cold deserts

quiz.q: Which animal helps people carry loads in the cold desert of Ladakh?
quiz.explain: Yaks have long, thick hair and can live in Ladakh's freezing cold.
quiz.mistake: Picks a hot-desert or forest animal

quiz.q: Jaisalmer, the 'Golden City', is in which desert?
quiz.explain: Jaisalmer in Rajasthan stands in the Thar Desert. Its yellow sandstone buildings glow golden.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which desert Jaisalmer is in

teach.ask: Gappu fans himself: 'Is every desert hot and sandy? And does a camel keep water in its hump?'
teach.praise: Wow! Deserts are dry places that can be hot like the Thar or cold like Ladakh. And the camel's hump has fat, not water!
teach.nudge: What makes a place a desert? Is every desert hot?

learn.hook: Imagine a piece of land with sea all around it, coconut trees, and coral reefs full of colourful fish. Welcome to India's islands!
points: An island is land that has water all around it.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the Bay of Bengal. Their capital is Sri Vijaya Puram (earlier called Port Blair).
Lakshadweep is a group of small coral islands in the Arabian Sea. Its capital is Kavaratti.
Corals look like rocks or plants, but they are made by tiny sea animals. Coral reefs are home to many fish.
Barren Island in the Andaman Sea has India's only active volcano. Majuli in Assam is a huge island in the Brahmaputra river.

example.q: Lakshadweep and the Andaman Islands are both groups of islands. Think it through: how can you tell them apart on a map?
steps: Find India's west and east coasts.
Lakshadweep is in the Arabian Sea, to the west.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are in the Bay of Bengal, to the east.
example.answer: Lakshadweep is in the Arabian Sea (west); Andaman and Nicobar are in the Bay of Bengal (east).

learn.reallife: Fish, coconut and seafood are a big part of meals on India's islands, and many people work as fishers or in tourism.

items.text: Land with water all around it is an ___.
The capital of Andaman and Nicobar is Sri Vijaya ___.
Majuli is an island in the ___ river.

quiz.q: What is an island?
options: Land with water all around it
quiz.explain: An island has water on all sides, like the Andaman Islands in the sea.
quiz.mistake: Confuses an island with a coast that has water on only one side

quiz.q: In which sea are the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
quiz.explain: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in the Bay of Bengal, east of mainland India.
quiz.mistake: Mixes them up with Lakshadweep

quiz.q: Lakshadweep islands lie in the
quiz.explain: Lakshadweep is off the coast of Kerala in the Arabian Sea.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the east and west seas

quiz.q: Corals are made by
quiz.explain: Corals are built by tiny sea animals. Their hard skeletons form reefs over many years.
quiz.mistake: Thinks corals are rocks or plants

quiz.q: India's only active volcano is on
quiz.explain: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea has India's only active volcano.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where the volcano is

quiz.q: What is the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands now called?
quiz.explain: In 2024, Port Blair was renamed Sri Vijaya Puram.
quiz.mistake: Does not know Port Blair was renamed, or picks the capital of another place

quiz.q: Majuli is special because it is
options: a large island in a river
a coral island in the sea
quiz.explain: Majuli sits in the middle of the Brahmaputra river in Assam.
quiz.mistake: Thinks islands are found only in the sea

quiz.q: Which tree is very common on India's sea islands?
quiz.explain: Coconut palms grow well in warm, sandy coastal places like Lakshadweep and the Andamans.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tree of cold mountains or the desert

teach.ask: Gappu lands on a rock in the sea: 'Is this an island? Which islands does India have?'
teach.praise: Hooray! An island has water all around. The Andamans are in the Bay of Bengal and Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea!
teach.nudge: What makes a piece of land an island? Can you name two of India's island groups?

learn.hook: Bridges made of living tree roots, a lake with floating islands, and the tallest mountains on Earth: India's wonders are real!
points: The Himalayas in the north are the highest mountains in the world. Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, stands on the border of Nepal and China.
Kangchenjunga, on the border of Sikkim and Nepal, is the third-highest peak in the world. You can see it from Sikkim and Darjeeling.
In hills, houses often have sloping roofs so that rain and snow slide off easily.
Mawsynram and Sohra (Cherrapunji) in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth. People there grow living root bridges from the roots of rubber fig trees.
Loktak Lake in Manipur has floating islands called phumdis. The rare sangai deer lives in a floating national park there.

example.q: Think it through: why do houses in Himachal Pradesh often have sloping roofs, while houses in the Thar Desert often have flat roofs?
steps: Himachal gets heavy rain and snow.
Sloping roofs let rain and snow slide off.
The Thar gets very little rain, so a flat roof works well and can be used for sleeping on hot nights.
example.answer: Sloping roofs suit places with lots of rain and snow; flat roofs suit dry places.

learn.reallife: On a trip to Shillong, you might cross a living root bridge. On a trip to Darjeeling or Sikkim, you might see snowy Kangchenjunga at sunrise.

games.title: Tallest first
games.prompt: Arrange these peaks from highest to lowest

items.q: Lake in Manipur with floating islands
World's third-highest peak, seen from Sikkim
Highest mountain range in the world

quiz.q: Which is the highest peak in the world?
quiz.explain: Mount Everest, about 8,849 m tall, is the highest peak on Earth. It stands on the border of Nepal and China.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the world's highest peak with other high Himalayan peaks

quiz.q: Kangchenjunga, the third-highest peak in the world, is in which Indian state?
quiz.explain: Kangchenjunga stands on the border of Sikkim and Nepal. Only Everest and K2 are higher.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where the big Himalayan peaks are

quiz.q: What are the floating islands of Loktak Lake called?
quiz.explain: Phumdis are floating masses of plants and soil on Loktak Lake in Manipur.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up phumdis with other landforms

quiz.q: Living root bridges are found in
quiz.explain: People in Meghalaya guide the roots of rubber fig trees across streams to grow strong living bridges.
quiz.mistake: Does not know this wonder of the north-east

quiz.q: Mawsynram in Meghalaya is famous for
options: getting a huge amount of rain
quiz.explain: Mawsynram is one of the wettest places on Earth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the wettest place with a desert

quiz.q: Why do houses in snowy hills have sloping roofs?
options: To catch more snow on the roof
So that snow and rain slide off
So birds can sit on them
quiz.explain: A sloping roof lets heavy snow and rain slide down instead of piling up.
quiz.mistake: Does not link roof shape with weather

quiz.q: The sangai, a rare deer, lives in which state?
quiz.explain: The sangai lives in Keibul Lamjao National Park on Loktak Lake, Manipur.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where the sangai lives

quiz.q: The Himalayas are in which part of India?
quiz.explain: The Himalayas stretch across the north of India, from Ladakh to Arunachal Pradesh.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Himalayas with the Western Ghats

teach.ask: Gappu shivers on a peak: 'Which is the tallest mountain? And what other wonders does India have?'
teach.praise: Unbelievable! The Himalayas, root bridges and floating islands. India is full of wonders!
teach.nudge: Which mountains are the highest? Can you tell me one more wonder, maybe in the north-east?
